nodes.label: implement-task-list Skill
nodes.rationale: Turn session-identified work into shared-list tasks, then hand each to a teammate that owns it from unread to open PR. Core principle: the lead delegates the work AND the paperwork - a teammate that does not claim its own task, invoke its own skills, and open its own PR is a pair of hands, not an owner, and the lead becomes the bottleneck. Seven-step pipeline including verifying the roster in config.json before teammates get deep, because a wrong roster is cheap to fix in the first minute and expensive after six agents have edited files.

nodes.label: Seven-Part Dispatch Contract
nodes.rationale: Every dispatch prompt carries: the task (TaskGet, claim via TaskUpdate), the goal in one sentence, the skills to use, scope (files owned and off limits), verification commands, the terminal deliverable stated in full, and close-out (TaskUpdate to completed plus a report). Parts 1, 3 and 6 are the ones that get dropped.

nodes.label: Terminal Deliverable Settlement
nodes.rationale: Opening a PR is outward-facing, so an agent will correctly refuse it by default and end at 'committed on your branch' - the single most common way the workflow ends half-finished. Ask once before dispatching, for the whole batch, and state the answer explicitly in every dispatch prompt; per-teammate or unstated is how three branches land and two sit unpushed.

nodes.label: Shared-Checkout Isolation
nodes.rationale: Never pass isolation: 'worktree' when spawning a teammate - it routes the Agent call down the ordinary-subagent path and what comes back never enters members[], gets no TaskGet/TaskUpdate, has no mailbox, and never appears in the console; nothing errors. Isolation comes from disjoint file ownership named in the dispatch prompt: each teammate stages its own paths by name (never git add -A), one shared branch created by the lead (they share HEAD, so git checkout -b moves everyone), never fix another teammate's file, retry on index lock.
